County the Metropolitan Districts Must File Annual Report With Douglas County

sources.text: Important Contact Information Community-Related Emergencies Emergencies: For any life-threatening emergencies, please call 9-1-1. If you have a community-related emergency, such as an irrigation leak or community space safety hazards, please call the Resident Resource Center at 720-661-9694 and press 2 for after-hours emergency services. Service requests or issues: Please use the Sterling Ranch 311 app to report a service request or issue. STERLING RANCH 311 Submit service requests or issues from your mobile device or computer on our 311 app. It's easy! Learn more here . sources.text: Trash & Recycling Our trash provider is Waste Connections. Waste Connections uses automated trucks to service Sterling Ranch and provide a more efficient trash and recycling experience. The new equipment features a side arm system that makes it easier to maneuver, ensures driver safety, and allows for faster service. Trash and recycling service fees are included in your monthly CAB bill. Pick Up Schedule Make sure to place bins outside by 7 am for trash collection. Containers for pickup may be placed on the street or alleyway on the morning of pickup and must be returned to an appropriately screened location by the end of the pickup day. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various types of wildlife. Pro per trash cart storage is essential to the community and its inhabitants' safety. Extra or bulky items can be picked up by contacting Waste Connections at 303-288-2100. For Providence Village , trash is picked up weekly on Monday, and recycling is picked up every other Monday. For Ascent Village, trash is picked up weekly on Tuesday, and recycling is picked up every other Tuesday. For Prospect Village , trash is picked up weekly on Thursday, and recycling is picked up every other Thursday. Holiday Schedule Trash pickup will be delayed by one day for the following holidays: New Year's Day Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Christmas Opt-In for Service Notifications Waste Connections also has an emergency phone call system that can notify residents in case of a delay or interruption in service. Service Notification Form New Homeowners Trash Cart Delivery Trash and recycling carts will be delivered to your home within ten days of closing.

sources.text: Recycling Right -- 1 of 13 -- Recycling Guidelines  Waste Connections uses a single stream recycling model.  All acceptable recycling materials can be placed in one container  No sorting required. -- 2 of 13 -- -- 3 of 13 -- Non-Recyclable Items  Chip Bags  Candy Wrappers  Napkins  Paper Plates  Tissues  Pizza Boxes  Plastic Grocery Bags -- 4 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes?  From your home to the Recycling Center.  From the Recycling Center to the Manufacture.  From the Manufacture back to you. -- 5 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes  Once your recycle has been cleaned and sorted inside your home and placed in your recycle container it is picked up by a Waste Connections recycle Truck and heads to EcoCycle. When the truck reaches EcoCycle it is put on a large conveyer belt and the sorting process starts. Plastic, paper products, metal and glass are sorted from each other. Once all the plastics have been sorted together, they are then sorted again by type. Plastic bottles used for water and soda go one way and milk containers go in another and so forth. This is done for paper, glass and metal as well. Once everything has been sorted, the different types of materials are bundled together in big cubs at a certain weight and are ready to be sold and shipped.  The cleaner the materials are the better. This allows for fewer issues with the sorting equipment and a better price. One contaminated recycle container can cause the entire truck load of material to be deemed contaminated and sends the entire load to the landfill.

sources.text: According to the EPA, here are the environmental and economic benefits of using landfill gas:  ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a safe and renewable energy source.  Using landfill gas reduces the need to use more polluting forms of energy.  Using landfill gas reduces health and community risks, such as air pollution.  Landfills that use their landfill gas tend to be better managed and make better neighbors. -- 9 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit BENEFITS  ECONOMIC BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a cost-effective, reliable, and local source of energy.  Using landfill gas can generate economic benefits for the community.  Developing and maintaining a landfill gas energy project creates local jobs.  A landfill with good power potential can attract business to the community. -- 10 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  According to the EPA, “When municipal solid waste is first deposited in a landfill, it undergoes an aerobic (with oxygen) decomposition stage when little methane is generated. Then, typically within less than 1 year, anaerobic conditions are established and methane-producing bacteria begin to decompose the waste and generate methane.  Landfill gas (LFG) is a natural byproduct of the decomposition of organic material in landfills. LFG is composed of roughly 50 percent methane (the primary component of natural gas), 50 percent carbon dioxide (CO2) and a small amount of non-methane organic compounds. -- 11 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  CONVERTING LANDFILL GAS TO ENERGY  Instead of escaping into the air, LFG can be captured, converted, and used as an energy source.

sources.text: Using LFG helps to reduce odors and other hazards associated with LFG emissions, and it helps prevent methane from migrating into the atmosphere.  LFG is extracted from landfills using a series of wells and a blower/flare (or vacuum) system. This system directs the collected gas to a central point where it can be transported, compressed, and filtered before it is combusted to generate electricity. -- 12 of 13 -- In Conclusion  Recycling right is the best way for Americans to protect the environment and stimulate the economy.  Recycling saves resource and reduces pollution.  Recycling is a shared responsibility.  Its easy! -- 13 of 13 --

sources.text: Water & Sewer Sterling Ranch water is provided by Dominion Water and Sanitation District, a wholesale water district serving Northwest Douglas County. To meet water demands, Dominion has contracts for permanent water delivery from Aurora Water, the Water Infrastructure and Supply Efficiency (WISE) project, and Castle Rock. Today, our water from contracts with the City of Aurora is delivered directly to the Larry D. Moore Water Treatment Plant, a facility jointly funded by Dominion and Roxborough Water and Sanitation District. Sterling Ranch: A Water-Wise Community The Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board ( CAB ) is committed to providing our residents with the highest quality tap water and reliable services. Sterling Ranch is part of a new approach to creating a regionally integrated, comprehensive water system with a robust, reliable, and renewable water supply. Dominion Water and Sanitation District and Sterling Ranch CAB have constructed a state-of-the-art water system, including a joint treatment facility with Roxborough Water and Sanitation District, the Larry D. Moore Water Treatment Plant. It is the first treatment plant in Colorado to receive 100% of its initial disinfection credits from Ultra Violet ( UV ) light and provides Sterling Ranch with clean, healthy water. Dominion Water and Sanitation District has been awarded a Certificate of Appreciation for being a WaterSense Partner by practicing and promoting water efficiency. Maintenance Checklist for a Water-Efficient Home Water & Sewer Billing After closing on their homes, Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer services. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears.

sources.text: To learn more about WaterSense, visit www.epa.gov/watersense. 832-F-24-002 March 2024 Do This Once Per Year to Save Water:  Check your home for leaks (indoors and outdoors) and repair them promptly. Find instructions on WaterSense’s website at www.epa.gov/watersense/fix-leak-week.  Make sure your toilets aren’t continuously running. Check for leaks by putting a few drops of food coloring in the tank and wait 10 minutes; if color appears in the bowl, you have a leak. Flush afterwards to avoid staining.  Inspect showerheads and faucets for scale buildup and clean if necessary. Add new plumbing tape to ensure a tight fit.  Add mulch as needed over landscaped areas in your yard.  Check your irrigation system for breaks and leaks, signs of overwatering or underwatering, and areas of overspray, and repair or adjust as necessary. See WaterSense’s Sprinkler Spruce-Up web page at www.epa.gov/watersense/sprinklerspruce-up and Watering Tips web page at www.epa.gov/watersense/watering-tips.  Test your pool’s automatic refill system and fill valve.  Winterize your irrigation system and pool to prepare for cold weather.  Check your service water pressure and adjust or replace your pressure-regulating valve if necessary.  Have a professional service your home’s water heater and water softener (if one is installed). If you like to do it yourself, make sure to flush your water heater to reduce sediment buildup; check the water heater’s temperature and pressure valve; and clean your water softener’s brine tank. Check These Areas More Frequently for Water Waste: Daily  Turn off faucets and hose bibbs unless you are actively using water.  Run only full loads of laundry and dishes and skip extra rinse cycles.  During swim season, cover your pool when it’s not in use.

sources.title: Water Billing
sources.text: Water Billing Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer after closing on their homes. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears. American Conservation and Billing Solutions ( AmCoBi) administers the monthly water bill each month. Questions? AmCoBi's Client Care Services Team is available to assist you with questions or concerns regarding your water bill. Please contact them at: Toll-free: 1-833-SRCAB-40 or (833) 772-2240 E-mail: ClientCare@AmCoBi.com Payment Options: Please register your account through Utility Hawk ( https://srcab.utilityhawk.us ). Point your Web browser to: https://srcab.utilityhawk.us/login Select the "Pay Online" link on the home page. Follow the instructions. Your online account allows you to choose the best payment options for you, check your account balance and activity, and elect to receive your water bill electronically (eBill). AmCoBi's ePay service allows you to pay your bill online with an automatic withdrawal from your checking/savings account (ACH) free of charge. You can also use a debit or credit card with a processing fee of 2.95%, charged by Paymentus, the payment processing provider. Report a Water Concern If you have concerns or questions about the water in your home, please complete the Report a Water Concern Form and a staff member will be in touch with you. Contact Us Resident Resource Center info@sterlingranchcab.com Physical Address 8220 Piney River Avenue Sterling Ranch , CO 80125 Phone: 720-661-9694 Emergency Phone: 720-661-9694 Ext. 2

sources.title: Rent the Facility
sources.text: Rent the Facility The Overlook Clubhouse is an excellent venue to host your event. It provides a perfect location and a fantastic atmosphere for any occasion. The clubhouse is an ideal gathering space for organizing events, parties, community meetings, activities, picnics, groups, and clubs. The Member Services team at the Overlook Clubhouse will assist you in making your private party an event for you and your guests to remember! Great Hall The Overlook Clubhouse offers a Great Hall with a warming kitchen, an outdoor deck, and an indoor/outdoor fireplace. This space can be reserved for private use. However, when not reserved, the Great Hall, kitchen, and outdoor deck are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Please note that all members of the private rental must remain in the rented space, and additional facility access will not be permitted. Hourly Pricing $100.00 per hour with a 2-hour minimum. All rentals include the use of the indoor space and balcony. A refundable security deposit of 250.00 will also be due upon rental confirmation. Outdoor Pavilions The clubhouse has two outdoor, covered pavilions to reserve for private parties. The pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved for private use. Each household can reserve one of the outdoor pavilions once per day, with no more than two rentals per calendar month. All members of the private rental must stay in the rented space. Additional facility access is not permitted. North Pavilion Larger space that includes an outdoor fireplace and convertible picnic tables South Pavilion Smaller space that includes an outdoor BBQ grill and two picnic tables Hourly Pricing $25 per hour.

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Water 6 All Content What does the monthly fixed fee include? The water rate billing structure includes a fixed monthly water service base fee and a residential usage charge. This base fee covers the cost of the water and sewer utility’s fixed and operating costs before any service is provided. The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies. Water How are my indoor water usage tiers established? A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC .

sources.text: Water How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Why are outdoor water rates slightly higher than indoor water rates? The water rates are structured to recover system costs. Outdoor water rates were designed to encourage water-wise irrigation practices. Outdoor water use increases the demand on our water system, and therefore the operational costs of our facilities. Additionally, when water is used outdoors it is fully consumed and not returned to the system. Water How do I move into higher tiers each month? The first tier of fee rates per 1,000 gallons applies to the use of up to 100% of the customer’s water budget. The tier fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100% of the water budget increases based upon the amount over 100% that is used by that customer.

sources.title: FAQs - CivicPlus.CMS.FAQ
sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Water 6 All Content What does the monthly fixed fee include? The water rate billing structure includes a fixed monthly water service base fee and a residential usage charge. This base fee covers the cost of the water and sewer utility’s fixed and operating costs before any service is provided. The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies. Water How are my indoor water usage tiers established? A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC .

sources.text: Water How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Why are outdoor water rates slightly higher than indoor water rates? The water rates are structured to recover system costs. Outdoor water rates were designed to encourage water-wise irrigation practices. Outdoor water use increases the demand on our water system, and therefore the operational costs of our facilities. Additionally, when water is used outdoors it is fully consumed and not returned to the system. Water How do I move into higher tiers each month? The first tier of fee rates per 1,000 gallons applies to the use of up to 100% of the customer’s water budget. The tier fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100% of the water budget increases based upon the amount over 100% that is used by that customer.

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool. White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool.

sources.text: Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches. Pool mattresses or other inflatables are prohibited. Users with noncompliant inflatables or flotation devices will be asked to remove them from the pool. Personal sound equipment, such as stereos or wireless speakers, are permitted as long as they do not disrupt others' enjoyment of the pool. If any complaints are received, Users will be asked to turn down their music, use headphones, or upon repeated complaint, asked to turn off the device or leave the pool. The pool must be cleared during thunder and lightning storms or other inclement weather events that present danger to Users.

sources.text: Each household receives 25 guest passes each calendar year linked to your CIVICREC account. Each CAB Resident household is permitted up to six (6) guests per day. If the Clubhouse and Pool is not at capacity, additional guests beyond six (6) will be permitted for a fee of $5.00 per guest. CAB Residents are encouraged to call and verify capacity before arrival. Overlook Clubhouse Pool Can a caregiver take my kids to the pool? You can purchase a caregiver pass for $300.00 for the calendar year, listing up to four names to use the caregiver pass. sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool. White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool.

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Home - FAQs 6 All Content How do I submit an application for Design Review? Please submit your completed application digitally via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com Design Review Committee (DRC) meetings are scheduled for the first and third Thursday during the months of March through September, and the first Thursday during October through February. Applications and forms can be downloaded on the DRC Applications web page . Completed applications must be received via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com by end of business day on the Friday prior to a DRC meeting to be reviewed at that meeting. If it is not received by end of business on the Friday before the meeting, it will be put on the following meeting’s agenda. If a fee is required, mail the physical check made out to Sterling Ranch Community Authority along with a copy of your application to Sterling Ranch DRC, 8155 Piney River Avenue, Suite 150, Littleton, CO 80125. Home - FAQs How do I pay my bill? Water & Sewer Bill: Residents of Sterling Ranch receive a monthly water & sewer bill in the mail each month. To view and pay your monthly water & sewer bill follow the following instructions: You have on-line access to all your water and CAB Services billing information.

Recurring credit card payments with Smartstreet are valid for one year or when your credit card expires, whichever is sooner. At that time, you must renew your payment with Smartstreet, it does not happen automatically. Click "More Details" to view the full event description, event cost, suggested ages, and registration links. Review the event details and confirm if an RSVP or program registration is required. If required, a link to register on the right-hand column will say "Register Now" Follow the registration prompts.

sources.text: The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies. Water How are my indoor water usage tiers established? A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC . Water How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves.

The tier fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100% of the water budget increases based upon the amount over 100% that is used by that customer. With thousands more homes coming in the next few decades, it is important for the community to adopt this new technology now instead of waiting for even more homes to come online with the current technology. sources.text: Once the Siemens technician arrives at your home, the equipment upgrades should take approximately 2 hours. Water Communication Retrofit Will I be able to use internet while the upgrade is taking place? The technician will need to shut off a circuit breaker to perform the necessary electrical work. If your internet is utilizing that same circuit breaker, you will not be able to access the internet for approximately 45 minutes while electrical work is being performed. Because of this, we strongly recommend not scheduling critical tasks that will require internet access or VoIP phone use during your service window. Water Communication Retrofit What can I do to prepare? In order to minimize the time required, prior to the technician’s arrival please clear adequate space (at least 3 square feet) around your water meter panel, electrical breaker box, and STEWARD equipment. This equipment is typically located in the basement. If you do not have a basement, the equipment is typically located in the garage. Water Communication Retrofit What information should I be ready to share? If you have changed the default login to your CenturyLink ONT /modem’s admin portal, please be prepared to provide that information as well. If you would prefer not to share this information, please be prepared to input your credentials for the technician at the necessary times. If you do not know your STEWARD login credentials, visit the Lumiere website . Water Communication Retrofit Why are you removing the virtual private network (VPN) hardware? The virtual private network ( VPN ) hardware was previously necessary to ensure proper encryption of water meter information during transmission to the water billing system. This is no longer the case as we are now able to use an alternate encryption method.

sources.text: Application fees can be paid via check made payable to Sterling Ranch CAB, or via credit/debit card. Please contact the team at the Resident Resource Center for assistance paying via credit/debit card. Checks can be mailed or dropped off to Sterling Ranch CAB, 8220 Piney River Ave, Littleton, CO 80125. Design Review After I receive my approval, can I modify or deviate from my application slightly? Approval was granted based on the information the homeowner provided to the committee on the application. A new Design Review Application will need to be submitted should a homeowner need to make any changes to the original application. (EXCEPT for plant material selection as long as it is for water to water same) Design Review How long does the Design Review Process take? The Design Review Committee has up to 30 days to review a submittal from the date a completed submittal package was received at the Design Review Committee meeting. If you have not been notified in writing by the 31st day after the meeting, the submittal is deemed to be denied. It is the responsibility of the applicant to contact the Design Review Committee to determine the status of the submittal. Design Review How many days do I have to install my rear yard? The rear yard landscape must be completed within 120 days following your closing. A Winter Deferral Period for completion of rear yard planting is granted for closings from November 1 to April 30. Design Review Am I allowed to make changes to my grading or drainage? The DRC does not evaluate changes to grading or drainage. Applicants are to seek approval from the County and/or other appropriate governing bodies. The DRC is not responsible in any way for changes made to grading and/or drainage while installing landscaping or other improvements.

sources.text: All County and State code requirements are to be followed and are the sole responsibility of the homeowner. Design Review Do I need Design Review Committee approval for my fence installation? No, fences are installed on property lines and must meet the Sterling Ranch fence design specifications. A friendly reminder to always call 811 for a utilities/wire locate before ever digging for anything in your yard. Design Review Am I limited to the plants on the Pre-Approved Recommend Plant List? Sterling Ranch collaborated with Denver Botanic Gardens to research plantings that flourish in Colorado’s semi-arid climate. The concerted research effort trialed planting for water sustainability and resiliency and took form as a test garden planted on the property that was maintained and observed for three years. The recommend plant list is a great start to understanding the Sterling Ranch planting palette, but the Design Review Committee will review additional plant material requests. Design Review Am I limited to the landscape contractors on the Pre-Approved Landscaper List? No, you may work with a landscaper of your choice, but that professional landscaper will need to meet with our Architectural and Community Standards Director to become certified and approved. The approval process includes education on Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives and the Design Review process. Please note, inclusion on this list does not constitute the CAB’s endorsement of any of these companies. This list is only intended to identify the individuals that have attended the CAB’s required informational sessions regarding the Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives.

sources.text: Please see the Process for Design Review page for specific details. Learn more about Design Review Compliance Are there any guidelines I need to follow to have a temporary dumpster or a storage pod at my house? Please submit an Application for General Architectural Improvements to the Design Review Committee for approval. Include with the application timeframe for dumpster or storage pod to be at property. Please note, dumpsters and storage pods must be placed in your driveway and are not allowed on a public right-of-way per Douglas County officials. Compliance What is the guideline for having a recreational vehicle at my home? The maximum amount of time a Recreational Vehicle is allowed to be parked is three overnights (e.g., 72 hours) during any 7-day period for loading, delivery, and maintenance. Periodic movement of the vehicle for the purpose of circumventing this standard shall not qualify the vehicle for an exception from this standard. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Article VI General Standards for further regulation details. Compliance Do I need to submit my paint colors even if I am painting my home the exact same colors? DRC approval is required, even if re-painting is being done with the same colors as the original or previous paint color. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Article VI General Standards for further regulation details. Compliance Do trampolines and play equipment require approval? DRC approval is required. Trampolines will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, setbacks from property lines, method of installation, and proposed safety netting. Trampolines are required to be anchored per manufacturer specifications.

sources.text: Compliance Is it okay for me to access the open space to do improvements on my property? No, all access to your property must be from the street side at the front of your home. Accessing the property through another lot, open space, parks, or landscaped tracts is prohibited. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Section IV. Landscaping Standards. Compliance What can I do about a barking dog or a neighbor that does not clean up after their animals on a regular basis? If you are trying to solve a problem with a barking dog or clean up after a pet, please start with communicating your concern to the pet owner or contact the following county authorities: Douglas County Animal Services, 303-660-7529, 7:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m. Sheriff’s Department Dispatch, 303-660-7500 (After 6 p.m. if an animal problem requires immediate attention). Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool.

sources.text: White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool. Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches.

sources.text: 8155 Piney River Ave #150, Littleton CO 80125 Billing Inquiries: Clientcare@amcobi.com Welcome, Sterling Ranch residents, to the most advanced water conservation community in Colorado. We are committed to conserving water and being good stewards of the land. Our innovative water solutions to conserve water community-wide will help residents with water costs long term. You play a part in this important conservation and we need your help. As you get your rear yards planted, we understand the need for an Establishment Period to promote healthy root system growth. This Rear Yard Establishment Period is a one-time only, 45-day period following the date of completion of your rear landscaping. Outdoor water used during this Rear Yard Establishment Period will be billed at the most affordable water cost, which is the “Tier One” water rate. In addition, the amount of water delivered during the Rear Yard Establishment Period will not count against your overall Water Budget. Please let the Community Authority Board know of your need for the Rear Yard Establishment Period water rates by completing the form below so that we make sure to ensure proper billing. This form can be mailed to the CAB at the address listed above or emailed to Clientcare@amcobi.com Name Address Phone Number Email Address Closing Date Account Number DATE OF TURF/VEGETATION COMPLETION OWNER SIGNATURE DATE CONDITIONS: 1. Due to the time needed to process this Notification, Tier One credits will be applied one time to your water bill at the end of the 45-day period. 2. Owners have 1-year to apply for Establishment Period credits. The 1-year period will start on the 120th day following Closing.

sources.text: Sterling Ranch Residential Property Owner Guidebook August 26, 2020 {00488209} Page 50 ATTACHMENT B-3 - REQUEST FOR LANDSCAPING INSPECTIONS The Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives * specify that soil amendment must be inspected prior to planting. This is to verify amendments have been incorporated into the soil in the quantity specified and to the depth required. Per the Water Demand Management Initiatives, the specification is 4 cubic yards of soil amendment for each 1000 square feet, tilled to a depth of 6 inches. Soil Amendment must be a combination of aged ground manure and compost. A second inspection will be performed after irrigation and plantings are complete in order to verify that the installed material is in substantial conformance with the approved plans, and that the irrigation system is active and in substantial conformance with the approved plans. The fee payment for these inspections is as follows: . $100.00 This fee covers both Soil Amendment Inspection and Landscape/Irrigation Inspection . Fee Payments should be made payable to Sterling Ranch Community Authority and sent to: Sterling Ranch Community Authority 8155 Piney River Ave, #150 Littleton CO 80125 TO SCHEDULE AN INSPECTION (MINIMUM 48 HOURS NOTICE, MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY ONLY): Contact residentialinspections@sterlingranchcab.com Provide your name, phone number, and email address plus the address of the property to be inspected. * If you do not have a copy of the Water Demand Management Initiatives, please visit www.sterlingranchcab.com to download the document. -- 1 of 1 --

sources.title: Application Landscape Professional_2023
sources.text: Sterling Ranch Code of Rules May 25, 2023 {00488209} Page 65 Registrations may be granted via reciprocity to individuals who hold registrations in other Colorado municipalities, on a case-by-case basis, as deemed appropriate by the Community Authority Board (“CAB”). AN APPLICANT MUST DEMONSTRATE THAT HE/SHE MEETS THE REQUIREMENTS BY PROVIDING CURRENT PROOF OF PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS. IN THE ABSENCE OF THESE CREDENTIALS, AN APPLICANT MAY SUBMIT A NARRATIVE LISTING THREE MOST RECENT PROJECTS, DOLLAR AMOUNT, COMPLETION DATE, AND CONTACT INFORMATION FOR THE PERSON FOR WHOM THE PROJECT WAS DONE. The CAB reserves the right to deny, suspend, or revoke any registration in accordance with its policies. ATTACHMENT G APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL OF LANDSCAPE PROFESSIONALS Registration requirements apply companies or organizations, not to individuals. The registered company or organization is responsible for all work performed under its supervision. Colorado law governs the sizes and types of projects that unlicensed individuals can design, and is independent from CAB policies. Registrations are valid for a period of three (3) years. Registration renewals for professionals in good standing may be issued upon receipt of acknowledgment of revisions to policies, criteria, or other applicable codes. sources.title: Calculating Outdoor Water Usage
sources.text: 8155 Piney River Avenue, #150 | Littleton Colorado 80125 submit@sterlingranchdrc.com Calculating Outdoor Water Usage for a Landscape Design Every home in Sterling Ranch has an outdoor water use budget based on the overall lot square footage. For water offered at the lowest, Tier 1 billing rate, see Table 1 below. . 30% of the outdoor water budget is used by the builder for the front yard irrigation . 70% of the overall outdoor water budget remains to irrigate the backyard plants . It is recommended to not design a landscape that requires 100% of the budget to allow for seasons with high temperatures and little precipitation conditions so that the Tier 1 billing rate is not exceeded. Calculate Outdoor Water Use Determine which plants in the plan are High Water, Moderate Water, and Low Water usage. Local nursery websites are a great resource to help understand the water needs of plants. Sod, vegetable gardens, and water features are always high water usage. Then, begin calculating the irrigated square footage (sf) of the plant by using the sf of each plant at full growth. See calculations below for some typical plant sizes. Trees are the exception to the rule. As water is only delivered around the trunk of the tree, use a 3’ diameter irrigated area for calculations. -- 1 of 2 -- 8155 Piney River Avenue, #150 | Littleton Colorado 80125 submit@sterlingranchdrc.com High Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 20 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season Moderate Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 10 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season Low Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 6 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season For example, a Moderate Water use plant at 2’ diameter full growth: 3.142 sf irrigated area x 10 gals/sf = 31.42 gallons needed for the season.

sources.text: The information on this sheet is NOT all inclusive of all Community Design Guidelines or Covenants. Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com OUTDOOR CONTROLLED PET AREAS DRC approval is required for all outdoor controlled pet areas including dog runs and kennels. . All outdoor controlled areas must be located in the side or rear yard, abutting the home and located behind yard fencing. . May not be located in a side yard adjacent to corner sidewalk, street, common area or open space. . Must be substantially screened from view by fast-growing plant material. Evergreen plantings and grasses are required for four season screening. . Required to be kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and not allowed to fall into disrepair. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various different types of wildlife. Always recommend, household pets including dogs and cats be kept indoors for their safety. Dog Run . A fenced, open-top area . May not exceed 200 square feet or more than 25% of the rear yard, whichever is less, . Constructed of fencing material matching that of lot-line fencing and stained to match lot-line fencing or may be black powder-coated steel not to exceed 48” in height from grade at any point. . Metal chain link enclosures are not permitted. . Pet mesh screen is required to be 2” x 4” galvanized welded wire mesh used on the inside of the fence, not to exceed the top rail in height, and continued down to ground level. . Covers (ex: tarps, sheets, blankets, etc.) are NOT allowed. Kennel . A free-standing panel-system kennel may not exceed 50 square feet and must be a maximum of 48 inches in height. .

sources.text: The information on this sheet is NOT all inclusive of all Community Design Guidelines or Covenants. Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com LANDSCAPE SCREENS DRC approval is required for landscape screens and will be considered based on the location of the screens, the size of your yard and the impact of screens on neighbors and the community. . 5’ maximum overall height for exposed landscape screen from grade. If plantings are installed at the base of the screen, facing out toward the community view, screen height will be allowed at a 6’ maximum overall height from grade. . 8’ maximum overall width for landscape screens. Multiple screens may not be attached at corners, at edges, to sheds, or to the house. Must be freestanding in the rear or side yard. . Landscape screens are only allowed in rear or side yards and are not allowed in easements. A maximum of three (3) screens are allowed if lot square footage permits. The DRC will review on a case by case basis. . Landscape screens must have 30% required transparency. . Materials must be constructed of a minimum 50% top grade redwood or cedar, or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home. If other materials like masonry or metal are used, they must match the architectural style of the house. Vinyl is not permitted. . Landscape screens may be either painted or stained. Paint colors must match or compliment house colors. Stain must match fence stain (Sherwin Williams #3002 Belvedere Tan) or a natural stain. Wood grain is allowed to show through. . Landscape screens may be used to screen hot tub areas on two sides only. .

Keep the neighborhood beautiful and completely screen unsightly trash and recycling bins from view from the street, the sidewalk or any adjacent property. DRC approval is NOT REQUIRED if ALL of the following conditions are met: . The trash enclosure/screening is installed behind the wing fence in the side yard (may not be on an exposed corner side), . Must be attached to the side of the house, . Has a minimum setback from the side property line of 5 feet, . Is not located within any easement(s), . Is constructed of top-grade cedar or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home or painted to match the fence stain color of Sherwin Williams #3002 “Belvedere Tan,” and . May not exceed 4’-6” in height from ground level at any point. Any trash enclosure/screening not meeting ALL of these conditions must be submitted for DRC approval. Trash and Recycling enclosures will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, and setbacks from property lines. Material, style and color, including roofing, need to be appropriate for the architectural style of the home. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various different types of wildlife! Proper trash cart storage is important to the safety of the community and those that inhabit it.

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Home - FAQs 6 All Content How do I submit an application for Design Review? Please submit your completed application digitally via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com Design Review Committee (DRC) meetings are scheduled for the first and third Thursday during the months of March through September, and the first Thursday during October through February. Applications and forms can be downloaded on the DRC Applications web page . Completed applications must be received via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com by end of business day on the Friday prior to a DRC meeting to be reviewed at that meeting. If it is not received by end of business on the Friday before the meeting, it will be put on the following meeting’s agenda. If a fee is required, mail the physical check made out to Sterling Ranch Community Authority along with a copy of your application to Sterling Ranch DRC, 8155 Piney River Avenue, Suite 150, Littleton, CO 80125. Home - FAQs How do I pay my bill? Water & Sewer Bill: Residents of Sterling Ranch receive a monthly water & sewer bill in the mail each month. To view and pay your monthly water & sewer bill follow the following instructions: You have on-line access to all your water and CAB Services billing information.

sources.text: Login to your Sterling Ranch Utility account at https://ebill.sterlingranchco.com/ubs1/ to: Pay your bill or setup an automatic payment Review your 12-month usage summary Understand your gallon consumption by month and year If you are having trouble locating your account number or need a copy of your bill please email info@sterlingranchcab.com Quarterly Assessment Bill: The quarterly CAB Service Fees are billed on a quarterly basis and are administered by Capital Consultants Management Corporation ( CCMC ). Quarterly CAB Service Fees include stormwater, trash and recycling, streetlights, and driveway maintenance (Lennar Elements homes only). Payment options are listed below. Direct-Debit The direct-debit payment option is available at no charge. If you are set up for direct-debit and your assessment has changed, the new amount will automatically be deducted. Download and complete the direct debit authorization form. Electronic Checks & Credit Card Payments To pay by Credit Card or Electronic, visit the Smartstreet Website . There is a $14.95 processing fee per credit card transaction. There is no charge for electronic check transactions. American Express, Discover, Mastercard, and Visa are accepted. Recurring credit card payments with Smartstreet are valid for one year or when your credit card expires, whichever is sooner. At that time, you must renew your payment with Smartstreet, it does not happen automatically. If you have recurring payments with Smartstreet and your assessment amount changes, you must update your payment information with Smartstreet as it doesn’t happen automatically. Bill-Payment Services If you use a bill-payment service please review your account number and payment mailing address.

sources.text: If you haven’t signed up to get access to the Overlook Clubhouse, complete the Resident Amenity Form online today! **For homeowners who registered for the Overlook Clubhouse prior to its opening in October 2020 should have received the email to complete account setup already. If you have not received the email or your link is expired, please contact the Overlook Clubhouse at 720-728-7257 or email recreation@sterlingranchcab.com and a staff member will assist you.** This account and password are for the new CIVICREC system and will be used for registering for events, reserving time to use the fitness center, purchasing fitness classes, additional guest passes, and more! Follow the instructions listed below to complete your account setup. How to Finish Your Online Account Setup Open the email. You will have a username (your email provided) and a temporary password to log in. Select TO LOGIN AND CHANGE YOUR PASSWORD NOW CLICK HERE. You will be redirected to the new CIVICREC Website. Once logged in, select ACCOUNT in the top lefthand corner. Select the pencil icon next to your name. In the lower-left corner, select RESET CIVICREC PASSWORD. You will be prompted to confirm that you would like to reset the password. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Follow the instructions to reset your password. Registering for Events & Programs Navigate to the Community Calendar . Click on the event that interests you. Click "More Details" to view the full event description, event cost, suggested ages, and registration links. Review the event details and confirm if an RSVP or program registration is required. If required, a link to register on the right-hand column will say "Register Now" Follow the registration prompts.

Home - FAQs How do I trouble shoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Home - FAQs Home - FAQs 6 How do I submit an application for Design Review? sources.title: STEWARD Home Automation System
sources.text: STEWARD Home Automation System STEWARD is your Smart Home Automation System and tightly integrated with all your other in-home devices. It’s an all-in-one home automation, home security, and utility monitoring system that came standard with your new Sterling Ranch home. STEWARD works with voice control, smart thermostats, door locks, garage doors, security cameras, and more. Standard Features Real-time, hourly & monthly reporting of your natural gas, electric & water usage A Rachio smart irrigation controller configured to water your lawn efficiently A DSC home security system that is connected to the STEWARD system Automated lighting and HVAC controls Connection to the Sterling Ranch Community to keep you informed about what’s happening around the neighborhood! Technology Help Open a Support Ticket

sources.title: Pickleball Courts
sources.text: Pickleball Courts Pickleball Facility Guidelines Hours and Reservations Hours: Weekdays 7 am-dusk; Weekends 8 am-dusk. Courts are located at Sterling Ranch Ave. and Middle Fork St. Free street parking is available near the courts. No pets are allowed inside the courts. Courts are available for reservations and drop-in play. Courts opened for play on August 1, 2025. Court reservations can be made for a maximum of two hours/day via the Sterling Ranch CAB CourtReserve portal or CourtReserve phone app. Residents can make reservations up to seven days in advance. Non-residents can make reservations up to three days in advance starting September 1, 2025. Residents: Free Non-residents: $40/court for up to four players Open play for non-residents: $20 for two players. Open play hours: Mon-Fri: 7-11 am, 5 - 8 pm. Sat-Sun: 8-11 am, 5 - 8 pm. Reservation hours: Mon-Fri: 11 am-5 pm. Sat-Sun: 11 am-5 pm. Tournaments and lessons held by Sterling Ranch CAB take precedence. Court Reserve Court Reserve is a web-based pickleball court reservation application to make it easier for members to reserve pickleball courts, and register for open play from a web browser or phone app. Click here for details on setting up your account. General Information Follow USA Pickleball rules for behavior and etiquette. (Click here to view the rules.) Be courteous; all skill levels are welcome. Bring your own paddles and balls. Tennis or court shoes required. Courts are for pickleball only-no skateboards, bikes, pets, etc. Courts are for personal play only. Paid or private events are prohibited. CAB-organized recreational programming is allowed. No ball machines, generators, chairs, tables, or glass items on courts. Dispose of trash, avoid sitting or leaning on nets/posts. Courts may be slippery when wet.

sources.title: Energy Crash Course Education Program
sources.text: Energy Crash Course Education Program Introducing the Energy Crash Course email education series, created exclusively for Sterling Ranch residents! Learn about important energy topics and how you can reduce your energy footprint This monthly email education program was designed to give you an in-depth overview of a different residential energy topic every month for a year, making it easy for you to learn how you can do your part in helping Sterling Ranch meet our Energy Action Plan goals of: 100% renewable electricity by 2030 Carbon neutral energy supply by 2040* The purpose of the program is to make it easy for Sterling Ranch residents to get involved in our community’s Energy Action Plan by learning more about how our energy system and technologies work. As a subscriber you’ll also find opportunities to engage with the services that our community partners Copper Labs and Xcel Energy provide, and receive simple, actionable tips on how to reduce your household energy use and support renewable energy! It will be a collective effort to meet our energy goals, but this program aims to equip our community with the background knowledge necessary to feel confident in the energy actions that we make and progress together in our efforts to practice sustainable energy stewardship! SIGN UP HERE Can’t wait a whole year or want to learn at your own pace? You’re in luck! You can access every email in the Energy Crash Course series below.

sources.text: Annual Drinking Water Consumer Confidence Report: Calendar Year 2021 general information Dominion Water and Sanitation District (Dominion) is the whole sale water supplier to the CAB. Unlike other water providers, Dominion’s supply starts with renewable water. In 2021, Dominion received water through contracts with the City of Aurora. Water is diverted from the South Platte River at Strontia Springs Reservoir and then runs through the City of Aurora’s tunnel to the Rampart Reservoir and transmission pipelines to the Moore Water Treatment Plant. Once it reaches the treatment facility, a number of treatment processes are utilized including coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection. The sources of drinking water include lakes, rivers, streams, ponds, reservoirs, springs, and wells. In order to ensure that tap water is safe to drink, Colorado Department of Health and Environment (CDPHE) prescribes regulations limiting the amount of certain contaminants in water provided by public water systems. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations establish limits for contaminants in bottled water that must provide the same protection for public health. Results from water quality tests confirm that your drinking water complied with all EPA drinking water standards in 2021. The following information and tables represent levels of regulated and unregulated water quality parameters sampled in 2021. Note: as previously reported, our maintenance contractor had one minor violation in 2021 due to a winterized backflow preventer that was not tested in accordance with the required schedule. The concern was corrected immediately upon de-winterization and at no time was there a public safety concern.

For more information about contaminants and potential health effects, or to receive a copy of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control (CDC) guidelines on appropriate means to lessen the risk of infection by Cryptosporidium and microbiological contaminants call the EPA Safe Drinking Water Hotline at (1-800-426-4791). The sources of drinking water (both tap water and bottled water) include rivers, lakes, streams, ponds, reservoirs, springs, and wells. As water travels over the surface of the land or through the ground, it dissolves naturally occurring minerals and, in some cases, radioactive material, and can pick up substances resulting from the presence of animals or from human activity. Contaminants that may be present in source water include: . Microbial contaminants: viruses and bacteria that may come from sewage treatment plants, septic systems, agricultural livestock operations, and wildlife. . Inorganic contaminants: salts and metals, which can be naturallyoccurring or result from urban storm water runoff, industrial or domestic wastewater discharges, oil and gas production, mining, or farming. . Pesticides and herbicides: may come from a variety of sources, such as agriculture, urban storm water runoff, and residential uses. . Radioactive contaminants: can be naturally occurring or be the result of oil and gas production and mining activities. . sources.text: In order to ensure that tap water is safe to drink, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment prescribes regulations limiting the amount of certain contaminants in water provided by public water systems. The Food and Drug Administration regulations establish limits for contaminants in bottled water that must provide the same protection for public health. Lead in Drinking Water If present, elevated levels of lead can cause serious health problems (especially for pregnant women and young children). It is possible that lead levels at your home may be higher than other homes in the community as a result of materials used in your home’s plumbing. If you are concerned about lead in your water, you may wish to have your water tested. When your water has been sitting for several hours, you can minimize the potential for lead exposure by flushing your tap for 30 seconds to 2 minutes before using water for drinking or cooking. Additional information on lead in drinking water, testing methods, and steps you can take to minimize exposure is available from the Safe Drinking Water Hotline (1-800-426-4791) or at epa.gov/safewater/lead. Source Water Assessment and Protection (SWAP) The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment may have provided us with a Source Water Assessment Report for our water supply. For general information or to obtain a copy of the report please visit wqcdcompliance.com/ccr. The report is located under “Guidance: Source Water Assessment Reports”. Search the table using 118021, DOMINION WSD, or by contacting ANDREA COLE at 720-531-4210 . The Source Water Assessment Report provides a screening-level evaluation of potential contamination that could occur. It does not mean that the contamination has or will occur.

sources.text: Maximum Residual Disinfectant Level (MRDL) − The highest level of a disinfectant allowed in drinking water. There is convincing evidence that addition of a disinfectant is necessary for control of microbial contaminants. . Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG) − The level of a contaminant in drinking water below which there is no known or expected risk to health. MCLGs allow for a margin of safety. . Maximum Residual Disinfectant Level Goal (MRDLG) − The level of a drinking water disinfectant, below which there is no known or expected risk to health. MRDLGs do not reflect the benefits of the use of disinfectants to control microbial contaminants. . Violation (No Abbreviation) − Failure to meet a Colorado Primary Drinking Water Regulation. . Formal Enforcement Action (No Abbreviation) − Escalated action taken by the State (due to the risk to public health, or number or severity of violations) to bring a non-compliant water system back into compliance. . Variance and Exemptions (V/E) − Department permission not to meet a MCL or treatment technique under certain conditions. . Gross Alpha (No Abbreviation) − Gross alpha particle activity compliance value. It includes radium-226, but excludes radon 222, and uranium. . Picocuries per liter (pCi/L) − Measure of the radioactivity in water. . Nephelometric Turbidity Unit (NTU) − Measure of the clarity or cloudiness of water. Turbidity in excess of 5 NTU is just noticeable to the typical person. . Compliance Value (No Abbreviation) - Single or calculated value used to determine if regulatory contaminant level (e.g. MCL) is met. Examples of calculated values are the 90 th Percentile, Running Annual Average (RAA) and Locational Running Annual Average (LRAA). . Average (x-bar) − Typical value. .

sources.text: Homeowner Landscape Class Any Property Owner planning to install landscaping and/or irrigation himself/herself must attend a training session. Landscape submittal plans will not be reviewed until the Property Owner can provide his/her Certificate of Training document. Homeowner Landscape Classes are taught March - September. For information or to register for the next class check out our community calendar. COMMUNITY CALENDAR

sources.title: 2023 Annual Meeting Presentation and Notes 12-12-2023
sources.text: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board 2023 Annual Meeting December 12, 2023 -- 1 of 29 -- Did You Know 2123 new homes closed through December 7th with another 22 expected to be closed in December. Yep, Sterling Ranch is still the #1 in Colorado. -- 2 of 29 -- Construction Planning, design, and bidding of Prospect Park with the Resident Advisory Committee. Construction commencing in 2024 and opening in 2025. -- 3 of 29 -- -- 4 of 29 -- -- 5 of 29 -- Construction We’ve identified a location to begin due diligence for the installation of pickleball. Due diligence in 2024, budgeting for 2025 with construction early in 2025. -- 6 of 29 -- Construction The Resident Advisory Committee has identified the existing splash pad at the Overlook as an area in need of update and is working on renovations to this key amenity! -- 7 of 29 -- Construction Warranty work from contractors is managed so that roads and streets can be turned over for maintenance to Douglas County at the end of the two-year warranty period. This saves CAB taxpayers money. -- 8 of 29 -- Inspections CAB Inspectors perform quality assurance on road (asphalt and concrete), water lines, sewer lines, landscapes, and other construction activities that are public infrastructure. Those inspections ensure that the public infrastructure is built according to plans and satisfactorily. -- 9 of 29 -- Landscaping New landscapes were installed in Prospect Village tree lawns and medians (Waterton Road, Mount Ouray Road, and Monte Vista Avenue). Tree lawns along Middle Fork Avenue in Ascent Village were installed this fall. -- 10 of 29 -- Lifestyle Why do people live in a community? While there are a lot of reasons, much of it has to do with lifestyle.

sources.text: Ranch Life events have proven to be a hit and enhance the desirability and livability of Sterling Ranch. Meet your neighbors and have some fun. -- 11 of 29 -- Lifestyle -- 12 of 29 -- Welcome! Coming December 29th! -- 13 of 29 -- Weekly Ranch Life E-Blasts Keep you in the know. Don’t receive them, go to this link to sign up: -- 14 of 29 -- Funding and Saving You Money CAB secured a commitment from Douglas County to contribute $2.5 million for the construction of Prospect Park. We are grateful to our Douglas County Commissioners for their support. -- 15 of 29 -- How Do We Pay for Public Infrastructure? The CAB was created to design, acquire, construct, install, finance, operate and maintain the public improvements for the entire Community. Public improvements generally consist of street, sidewalk, alleys, water, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, park, recreation, and landscape improvements. -- 16 of 29 -- How Do We Pay for Public Infrastructure? CAB finances and pays for the construction of Public Improvements through a combination of debt instruments such as publicly sold, taxexempt, bond issuances or developer financed advances that are later converted into bonded indebtedness or paid back out of bond proceeds. -- 17 of 29 -- CAB Issued Bonds CAB DEBT FACTS: o CAB may issue debt to fund the actual capital costs of constructing public improvements as required for the phasing and build out of the entire development. o Any debt must be amortized over a period not to exceed 40 years.

sources.text: Q: Is the CAB certified to inspect the streets and other areas that they build and does Douglas County recognize our inspections? A: Inspections are carried out by both CAB personnel and Douglas County. Each entity inspects for different reasons. The CAB inspects the public infrastructure that will be owned and maintained by the CAB, for example, the water and sewer mainlines. Both the CAB team and Douglas County inspectors inspect street, curb, gutter, and sidewalk improvements that will be accepted by the County. The CAB inspects to ensure the improvements are completed to contract specification, which includes County specifications. The County inspection is additional as they are certifying their acceptance of those elements as the County has long term operations and maintenance responsibility. Q: When can we look forward to seeing Burns Park built? A: Civil construction and grading will begin in Filing 7A in early 2024. Filing 7A is the west boundary of Burns Park. As that work progresses and is completed, portions of Burns Park will begin to be constructed, starting in the southern part of the park. Very shortly CAB will be asking Douglas County for $300,000 to start designing Burns Park as a "regional park.” Q: If we have another area of homes open for development, and we need bonds to fund construction, when do those bonds need to be paid and who pays for them? A: The CAB will issue bonds to support public infrastructure construction in the new areas. That area will be part of Metropolitan District 4 Subdistrict A. CAB will issue Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds that are supported by future property tax revenues in the Subdistrict.

sources.text: As with other parts of the community, payment of those bonds is subject to the 50 mils (as adjusted) debt service mill levy cap and counts towards the total community debt limit of $1,800,000,000. Those bonds are payable only by the properties in District 4 Subdistrict-A. Other CAB debt, specifically the Jr. Subordinate bonds, are supported by the pledge of revenues from all Sterling Ranch Metropolitan Districts and pay for costs that the CAB was not able to cover at the time of construction but that benefit the entire Sterling Ranch community. -- 27 of 29 -- Q: How many schools will we have? A: Douglas County School District will continue to monitor community growth and will determine ultimately how many schools will be in Sterling Ranch. Both CAB and the School District recognize the immediate need for an elementary school here in Sterling Ranch. As many of you are aware, the most recent School District capital improvement bonds to build schools failed. Therefore, the School District doesn’t currently have the funds to build a school here in Sterling Ranch. However, there are a other options that may expedite school construction such as a charter school. Q: Who ends up paying for the bonds? A: Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds are issued by the CAB and paid for through property taxes pledged by respective districts. All debt service payments are subject to the mill levy cap and total debt issuance limitation. Q: If we can issue up to $1.8B with 12,000 homes, with interest, how much will I as an individual owner wind up paying? A: The debt authorization limit includes debt beyond the initial buildout of the community to account for refunding, refinancing, or future capital development needs.

sources.text: You’ll never pay more than the 50 mil debt service cap, as adjusted, through your taxes. What will you pay over the life of living in your home? That’s open to many different factors, including the value of your home, the length of time you live in the community, impact of future bond refunding’s and future market conditions. The bonds are paid off over 30- or 40-year increments, and the benefit of funding infrastructure through bonds is that future residents pay for the costs of improvements as well as current residents, ensuring greater equity over time. Q: Can the CAB issue bonds without an election? A: There is not a requirement for a general election prior to debt issuance. The CAB, through the Districts, has debt authorization and pledge agreements that support debt issuance. Residents elect members to serve on the Metropolitan District Boards and the District Boards appoint members to the CAB Board. Q: Regarding the school parcels, are those currently owned by Douglas County or is that land sold by the development company? A: During the land planning process, a certain amount of land is determined to be used for open space, residential, commercial, and for schools. The County requires a certain dedications at certain population thresholds. As areas of the development are platted, land is dedicated to Douglas County for specific uses, like a library or schools. The land is not sold to the County. Q: Can you talk about all the other expenses that we pay as owners, water is expensive, trash, streetlights? -- 28 of 29 -- A: Costs for these items are based on expenses. For example, the Waste Connections contract has a built-in year over year increase, and that increase is passed on to the owners for the cost of the contract. Streetlights are very similar.
